transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Redwood CSM) -- CloudMesh: Jordan Rivers, Maya Lin, Tomas Vega, Luis Ortega, Hannah Cho

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
CloudMesh is evaluating Redwood as an inference partner to offer a managed onramp for third-party SaaS customers and to integrate Redwood Dedicated capacity into their marketplace offerings. Primary concerns: multi-tenant routing, KV cache compatibility with CloudMesh edge nodes, VPC/private deployment options, KMS integration for tenant keys, and pricing for reserved pilot capacity. Decided next steps: share SOC2 + network diagrams, Redwood to run pilot benchmarks on sample workload, schedule pilot kickoff early September.

Topics: integration architecture, security/compliance, pilot scope, latency & cost tradeoffs, routing/fallbacks, pilot timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um I'm Alex from Redwood AE team. We got Priya and Jordan on the call from engineering, quick intros?
[00:07] Jordan Rivers: yep hi I'm Jordan, Head of Partnerships at CloudMesh. Happy to meet you all.
[00:10] Maya Lin: Maya here, Integration Lead - I'm the one who will be doing most of the API work.
[00:15] Tomas Vega: Tomas, security architect. I'll be asking the usual questions around KMS, audit logs, and isolation.
[00:20] Luis Ortega: Luis, I run infra and SRE.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Priya, SE at Redwood - I focus on serving runtime and performance.
[00:29] Jordan Li: Jordan L., solutions eng, will help with the pilot plan.
[00:33] Marta Gomez: Marta, CSM, here to help with onboarding and timelines.

[00:40] Alex Chen: cool, thanks. Quick agenda — confirm goals, walk through architecture options (hosted, dedicated, private), talk security, then pilot scope and next steps. Sound good?
[00:46] Jordan Rivers: yep go for it.

[01:10] Priya Desai: so to frame, there are three patterns we typically see: 1) Redwood hosted API — low friction, good for quick onboarding; 2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools you can present in your marketplace as capacity; and 3) Redwood Private — VPC or on-prem for strict compliance. For CloudMesh marketplace you mentioned wanting tenant isolation and KMS keys per tenant, so Dedicated or Private are generally the fit.
[01:32] Maya Lin: right, our marketplace has tenant-level keys and we want to avoid passing cust data through a shared metal plane. Is Dedicated truly isolated? or is there any shared control plane?
[01:45] Priya Desai: Dedicated has isolated inference pools and data at-rest encryption per customer. Control plane can be either shared SaaS or private control plane — if you need total separation we offer private control plane + VPC peering or on-prem package. There is still a control plane but telemetry can be routed to your SIEM.

[02:10] Tomas Vega: about KMS: we require customer keys that we manage in our HSM. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM integrations and BYOK?
[02:20] Priya Desai: yes — Redwood Private supports BYOK with cloud KMS and HSM integrations. In Dedicated we can do KMS integrations as well but it depends on the deployment model. We'll share the KMS integration matrix in the security pack.

[02:52] Alex Chen: to add, we also have per-tenant audit logs, token-level tracing in the console, and the ability to forward logs to your Splunk/Datadog. We'll include sample log formats.

[03:20] Maya Lin: great. On the integration side, two technical constraints: 1) our edge nodes run a lightweight container and expect token passthrough with prefix caching — does Redwood's KV cache work with our edge flow? 2) we need a per-tenant routing policy so that some customers go to hosted to save cost, others to dedicated for SLA.

[03:46] Priya Desai: the KV cache — we do prefix + KV caching inside the runtime; there are two ways to do it with CloudMesh edge. Option A: Redwood handles KV caching centrally and you use a cache-aware header; Option B: we export a cache API shim so your edge can hold prefixes and we will hit the runtime with session continuations. Option B is new but we've prototyped it with a few partners.
[04:20] Luis Ortega: prototyped how? is there additional latency for Option B? our SLOs at the edge are tight, 50-100ms p50 for short responses.
[04:30] Priya Desai: Option B reduces repeated token decode across the wide area since the edge keeps prefix states; for very short responses it helps a lot. Right now the extra hop is minimal if you colocate the edge with a Redwood region — but we need to benchmark.

[05:05] Jordan Rivers: okay, pilot framing idea — we want Redwood to provide Dedicated capacity that we can resell to our customers, but start with a 3-week pilot focused on 10 tenants, low-traffic, to validate routing, billing, and KMS. Will that work?
[05:20] Alex Chen: yes that’s typical. We'll propose pilot capacity and pricing. Pilot includes: sandbox keys, routing policy test, 48-hour benchmark runs, and an eval of cost per token vs latency.

[05:45] Hannah Cho: on success criteria — for us the pilot must show: <1) per-tenant isolation verified, 2) latency within 1.5x of baseline for target workloads, 3) clear billing breakout per tenant, and 4) no customer PII leaving our VPC unless permitted.

[06:10] Priya Desai: understood — those map to our standard checklist. For privacy and data residency we can pin model variants to regions and enable TTL of caches.

[06:35] Tomas Vega: audit-wise we need immutable logs for 1 year and a legal-ready export format. Is Redwood's audit export S3-compatible and signed?
[06:45] Alex Chen: yes we support signed S3 exports and JSONL audit streams; we'll include retention options in the security docs.

[07:05] Maya Lin: switching to routing / fallback — if Dedicated capacity is saturated we want automatic fallback to lower-tier hosted models for burstability but with a label that surfaces in billing. Is that possible?
[07:20] Priya Desai: yes — smart routing policies can do that. You can set cost-first or latency-first policies and define fallback model families. We tag requests so you get clear billing and can trace model fallbacks.

[07:45] Luis Ortega: how do you handle model versions? if we pin to a particular model and Redwood rolls a quantized variant, what happens?
[07:55] Jordan Li: we support version pinning and we can do canary rollouts. If you pin, we won't auto-upgrade unless you opt in. For quantized variants we surface perf/quality metrics and a manual opt-in.

[08:30] Maya Lin: any guardrails for hallucination or quality regressions? we run some regen-evals on outputs with our test prompts.
[08:40] Priya Desai: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets; we can run evals during the pilot and create regression alerts. We'll need your test prompts — that is part of the benchmark plan.

[09:05] Tomas Vega: network layout: we prefer VPC peering from CloudMesh to Redwood Dedicated region rather than opening public endpoints. Is peering supported?
[09:15] Alex Chen: yes — VPC peering or private link is supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll include network diagrams and required CIDR ranges.

[09:40] Jordan Rivers: curious on pricing — how do you price Dedicated vs hosted for resale? gross margin expectations?
[09:50] Alex Chen: we'll send a pilot pricing sheet. High level: hosted is per-token; Dedicated is a committed monthly capacity fee + per-token overage. For resale we have partner programs with margin bands depending on commit size. We'll include an example TCO sheet in the follow-up.

[10:15] Hannah Cho: procurement will ask about SLAs and uptime for Dedicated. Typical SLA percentages?
[10:22] Marta Gomez: Dedicated SLA is usually 99.9% with options for 99.95% on enterprise contracts. We'll capture that in the pricing doc.

[10:40] Luis Ortega: let's talk about integration work — how long to get from pilot sign-off to pilot live? our timeline target is early Sept (~2 weeks).
[10:50] Priya Desai: if we get sample prompt sets and API spec this week, engineering can provision pilot capacity in ~5 business days and run the initial benchmarks in 48 hours. So early September is feasible.

[11:15] Maya Lin: small but important — billing and metering: we need per-tenant token counts and ability to map tokens to our tenant IDs. Do you expose token-level metering with tenant metadata?
[11:27] Jordan Li: yes, token-level metering with labels is available. We also provide per-route cost breakdown and can export usage as CSV or push to your billing endpoint.

[11:45] Tomas Vega: security nit: do you support SAML SSO for the Redwood Console and RBAC mapping to our org groups?
[11:53] Alex Chen: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM, and granular RBAC are supported. We'll send the SSO configuration guide.

[12:10] Maya Lin: any red flags on our side? we have customers that require data residency in EU only — can you pin?
[12:18] Priya Desai: yep region pinning is supported. For EU-only residency we'd recommend Redwood Private in your EU region or Dedicated capacity in our EU region with contractual data residency terms.

[12:40] Jordan Rivers: ok this is useful. I want to surface one internal constraint: some of our marketplace customers are very price-sensitive and will not accept dedicated pricing. We need a hybrid flow where lower-tier customers go to hosted and premium ones go to dedicated, transparently. You mentioned routing earlier; can that be policy driven from our side?
[12:58] Priya Desai: yes you can push routing policies via API — e.g., tenant metadata, SLA tier, or cost threshold. Policy engine can be managed by CloudMesh or via Redwood's console API.

[13:20] Alex Chen: quick note on benchmarking — we'll likely run the pilot harness with your sample workload, measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens across two model families and two quantization profiles. That will give you a TCO matrix to make resale decisions.

[13:45] Luis Ortega: and we'll want a CSV export of those results, ideally raw latencies and token counts.
[13:50] Jordan Li: absolutely, raw exports and summarized dashboards.

[14:05] (brief cross talk about exact prompt sets and where to store them)
[14:25] Maya Lin: note — we'll put prompts and a small synthetic dataset into a shared S3 bucket and give Redwood access. That should be done by tomorrow.

[14:40] Tomas Vega: final question from security: encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[14:45] Priya Desai: we support mTLS for private connections and TLS 1.3 for public endpoints. We'll put specifics in the security doc.

[15:05] Alex Chen: ok I want to summarize next steps quickly so we've captured it: Alex to send security pack + SOC2 + SSO guide; Priya to share benchmark plan and sample prompts list; Redwood to propose pilot pricing by Monday 8/24; CloudMesh to provision prompt S3 and API spec by 8/22; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 9/7. Any additions?
[15:30] Jordan Rivers: sounds good. Also include routing policy examples so our engineers can try a demo flow.

[15:40] Maya Lin: and include the cache shim docs for Option B, even if it's alpha.

[15:50] Alex Chen: will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.

[16:00] (meeting ends)

Recap (auto):
- Pilot: 3-week pilot for 10 tenants, capacity to be provisioned in Dedicated (or Private per residency), benchmark suite to run 48-hour, focus on routing, billing, KMS integration, and latency/cost metrics.
- Security: BYOK/HSM supported for Private, signed S3 audit exports, 1-year retention option, mTLS for private peering.
- Integration: KV cache shim option for edge prefix caching (alpha), API-level routing policies for tenant assignment, token-level metering and exports.
